ARITHMETIC LOGIC UNIT (ALU) - The ALU is an integrated circuit that contains adders, counters, registers and logic circuits. The ALU performs math operations (adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing) and logic functions (AND, OR, NOT).
DEFINITION
The ALU performs all math operations by using an adder circuit.
This lesson demonstrates how numbers are subtracted using an adder circuit.

LESSON MENU
A subtractor circuit is designed to subtract binary numbers. The subtraction is performed using an adder circuit.
DISCUSSION
Input A applies the minuend to the adder circuit.
DEFINITION
MINUEND - The minuend is the top number in a subtraction operation. For example, 5 is the minuend in this problem. The bottom number is called the subtrahend.
Input A applies the minuend to the adder circuit...........
Input B applies the subtrahend to the adder circuit.
DEFINITION
SUBTRAHEND - The subtrahend is the bottom number in a subtraction operation. For example, 3 is the subtrahend in this problem. The top number is called the minuend.
Input B applies the subtrahend to the adder circuit........
Notice, the B input passes through a circuit called two's complement.
The two's complement circuit inverts the B input and adds a one. Using the two's complement allows the adder to represent the difference between inputs A and B.
The only difference between adding and subtracting two numbers is that the two's complement of input B must be used.
Let's discuss two's complement to see how the adder is able to subtract binary numbers.
For the adder circuit to subtract binary numbers, the two's complement of the subtrahend must be used.
To find the two's complement, first invert the subtrahend. The ones are changed to zeros and the zeros are changed to ones.1
Then add one to the inverted subtrahend. This number is the two's complement.
Next, the adder will add the two numbers together. The carry indicates whether the answer is positive or negative.
When a carry is generated, the answer is positive. The carry is dropped.
When no carry is generated, the answer is negative. The two's complement of the sum is the final answer.
When no carry is generated, the answer is negative. The two's complement of the sum is the final answer.
You have just subtracted two numbers by using two's complement and adding them together.

Now that you have an understanding of the math process let's look at a subtractor circuit.
Two binary numbers are stored in registers A and B.
Inputs A and B are serial inputs that are gated into the adder on the leading edge of the clock pulse.
Input B is applied through an inverter. The inverter performs the complement function. The CI provides the additional one needed for the two's complement.
The CI is taken from the Q output of the D-type . The flip-flop starts with a high Q output due to the momentary high that is applied to the PRE input.RE input.
Once the addition process begins, the Q output changes as the CO changes.

A parallel subtractor circuit uses four adders to subtract a four bit binary number with one clock pulse.
Two binary numbers are stored in registers A and B.
The outputs of register B are applied through an inverter. This performs the complement function.
Note, the LSD adder is a full adder. CI is at +5 V to provide the one needed for two's complement.
The CO is used for the CI to the next adder.
The sum from each adder is shifted to register C. Note, the CO of the last adder becomes the MSD of register C.
For example, subtracting 1010 from 1110 equals 0100. Continue to observe the process.s.
